::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## How the page is built

`site/downloads/index.qmd` contains a Quarto listing over `site/downloads/downloads.yml`, using `site/downloads/downloads-table.ejs.md`. The YAML file is generated; do not maintain it manually.

Before every site render, `_quarto.yml` runs:

```powershell
python scripts/build_download_catalogue.py
```

Because the command runs from `site/`, the repository script is `site/scripts/build_download_catalogue.py`. It uses only the Python standard library and resolves paths from its own location.

## Inputs and output

The builder scans `site/downloads/files/metrics/**/catalogue/{release_id}.yml`.

It currently accepts `schema: bnr_download_manifest_v1` and `package_type: metric`. The central page lists entries whose download item has `include_in_listing: true`. Public links must remain under the permitted `files/` prefix and resolve to an existing ZIP package.

The single generated output is `site/downloads/downloads.yml`. It is rewritten only when its complete generated content changes. An unchanged message is normal after a rebuild that does not change catalogue metadata.

## Manual procedure

From the repository root:

```powershell
.\venv-info-hub\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python site/scripts/build_download_catalogue.py
```

Then:

1. Review `git diff -- site/downloads/downloads.yml`.
2. Start or refresh the Quarto preview.
3. Open `/downloads/` and locate the expected release.
4. Check its surveillance area, period, release date, description and ZIP link.
5. Open the ZIP and confirm it is the approved public package.
6. Run a complete site render.

## Failure safety

The script validates all source records and selected ZIPs before writing the central YAML. If any input fails, it exits without replacing an existing `downloads.yml`. Correct the source catalogue entry or package created by the publication workflow, then rerun. Never patch the generated central file to hide an invalid source record.

The builder indexes public packages only. It does not validate analytical values, approve releases, render Quarto, commit or deploy.
